name: Boston Brown Bread
description: Historical recipe from Common Sense in the Household (1871). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: potatoes, mashed fine with three cups of flour
ingredients.originalText: 6 potatoes, mashed fine with three cups of flour

instructions.text: Set a sponge over night with potatoes or white flour in the following proportions: 1 cup yeast, 6 potatoes mashed fine with three cups of flour, 1 quart warm water, 2 tablespoonfuls lard, 2 tablespoonfuls brown sugar
Beat up well and let it rise five or six hours
When light, sift into the bread-tray 1 quart rye-flour, 2 quarts Indian meal, 1 tablespoonful salt, 1 teaspoonful soda or saleratus
Mix this up very soft with the risen sponge, adding warm water if needed, and working in gradually half a teacupful of molasses
Knead well and let it rise from six to seven hours
Work over again and divide into loaves, putting these in well-greased, round, deep pans
The second rising should last an hour
Bake in a moderate oven about four hours
If put in late in the day, let it stay in the oven all night

source.author: Marion Harland
source.originalInstructions:
1. Set a sponge over night with potatoes or white flour in the following proportions: 1 cup yeast, 6 potatoes mashed fine with three cups of flour, 1 quart warm water, 2 tablespoonfuls lard, 2 tablespoonfuls brown sugar
2. Beat up well and let it rise five or six hours
3. When light, sift into the bread-tray 1 quart rye-flour, 2 quarts Indian meal, 1 tablespoonful salt, 1 teaspoonful soda or saleratus
4. Mix this up very soft with the risen sponge, adding warm water if needed, and working in gradually half a teacupful of molasses
5. Knead well and let it rise from six to seven hours
6. Work over again and divide into loaves, putting these in well-greased, round, deep pans
7. The second rising should last an hour
8. Bake in a moderate oven about four hours
9. If put in late in the day, let it stay in the oven all night
